newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Dec 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Dec 16.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not gaurantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.

- Government weighs plan to make economic retaliation against France for about-face on its decision to sell home appliance division of Thomson SA to Korea's Daewoo Electronics Co, terming the suspension of the Thomson privatization unfair action. French corporations would be restricted in bidding for Korea's arms procurement and nuclear power plant projects.
- Crime syndicate dealing with 200 billion won worth of fraudulent commercial papers in Korea's largerst port city of Pusan uncovered.
- Korean financial market put in disarray as stock market continues to tumble and foreign exchange rates soar. Concerns mount over Korea's further money market opening next year.
- Appeal sentences for former presidents Chun Doo Hwan, Roh Tae-woo, convicted of treason and mutiny charges in first trial, due today.
- China decides to accept long-term migration of North Korean people to help Pyongyang overcome economic problems, according to a Beijing source.
- Bond market to be opened up next year, allowing foreign investors to buy unguaranteed convertble bonds for small Korean businesses.
- Free trade port eyed in Kwangyang, 420 KM south of Seoul.
- Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchman arrived in Seoul yesterday for four-day visit.
